```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days. A has a short path to that: a $5–$20/month consumer purchase reached through $0-cash expat communities or ~$275 micro-influencer posts. B has a per-practice sales cycle reached through $1,850–$10,000 conference booths.",
    "B's own brief documents a near-identical precedent, Cydoc. Over seven years it reached four paying customers and $27,900 in revenue, most of it non-subscription. Integration cost $4,000–$6,000 per practice, and customers renegotiated scope practice by practice. That is direct evidence against landing a first customer quickly.",
    "B carries heavy ongoing compliance work that a solo founder must handle before the first sale: a HIPAA BAA for each customer, ongoing safeguards, and FDA non-device review. Physicians are also reluctant to trust AI notes that carry liability. A's COPPA/GDPR-K voice-consent burden is real but likely more contained.",
    "A's competitors publish consumer prices (Dinolingo $19.99/mo, Voiczy ~€7/mo, EveryLingo $5.99). That gives a sourced price anchor at a level where impulse purchases are plausible. B's anchor ($99/provider/month) is sourced, but B's 'apparent traction' claim for competitors is unsourced.",
    "AI agents can produce much of A's core asset cheaply: vocabulary, illustrations, TTS/ASR across language pairs. B's hard parts (EHR fit, trust, integration, sales) are not what agents solve, as Cydoc's founder put it: 'deploying health AI is only 20% of the challenge.'"
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's primary demand quote comes from a PMHNP who is an employee, not a practice owner or payer. She asked her employer for more patient paperwork, not software, and got no follow-up. It shows frustration but no purchase intent or budget. The other demand point is an AMA statistic relayed through a competitor's marketing page.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A's evidence is also thin. It has only two demand quotes, and one comes from a competitor's founders. It inherits a 100% paying-customer churn red flag from the seed SaaS, and Dinolingo reviews describe children zoning out. A wins mainly because B's brief contains strong documented counter-evidence (Cydoc) against fast first revenue, not because A's demand is well proven. A's churn risk matters more for sustainability than for getting the first paying customer in 90 days."
}
```
